TCGA breast cancer PI3K pathway expression, Normal vs Tumor

Source: R/data.R
brca_pi3k.Rd

RNA-seq expression of the 28 PI3K-pathway genes (Sanchez-Vega et al. 2018) in 100 normal breast tissue samples and 100 primary breast tumours from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) BRCA cohort. This is the dataset of the TCGA example in the DiNA simulation paper. It is shipped here so that spikeyglass, multiGGM and other packages use one identical object.

Usage

brca_pi3k

Format

A named list of two numeric matrices, Normal and Tumor, each 100 samples x 28 genes, with HGNC gene symbols as column names (in the same order in both). The attribute "genes" is a data frame with the columns Gene, og_tsg (oncogene / tumour suppressor / other, from Sanchez-Vega et al.) and pathway.

Source

The Cancer Genome Atlas, via the Bioconductor package curatedTCGAData (Ramos et al. 2020). The results here are in whole or in part based upon data generated by the TCGA Research Network: https://www.cancer.gov/tcga.

Details

Built by data-raw/brca_pi3k.R in the package sources:

  1. curatedTCGAData 2.1.1, BRCA RNASeqGene assay (BRCA_RNASeqGene-20160128, raw counts). Tumour = TCGA sample type 01, Normal = 11; the 3 metastatic samples are dropped.

  2. Genes with a count of at least 10 in fewer than 20\ dropped.

  3. DESeq2 variance-stabilising transformation (vst(blind = FALSE), design ~ sample_type).

  4. Each gene is z-scored across all Normal and Tumour samples together. The groups are therefore not standardised separately: within group, the Normal genes have standard deviations of about 0.7 and the Tumour genes about 1. Standardise within group (e.g. spikeyglass::ssjgl(standardize = TRUE)) if your method needs it.

  5. Normal samples, and tumours of patients without a paired normal sample, are kept, so the two groups come from different patients.

  6. The PI3K-pathway genes of Sanchez-Vega et al. (2018) are kept (28 of 29 pass the filters).

  7. The first 100 tumours (in the order produced by the pipeline, not a random sample) are kept to balance the 100 normals.

Sample identifiers are not included.

References

Cancer Genome Atlas Network (2012). Comprehensive molecular portraits of human breast tumours. Nature, 490, 61–70. doi:10.1038/nature11412

Sanchez-Vega, F., Mina, M., Armenia, J., et al. (2018). Oncogenic signaling pathways in The Cancer Genome Atlas. Cell, 173(2), 321–337. doi:10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.035

Ramos, M., Geistlinger, L., Oh, S., et al. (2020). Multiomic integration of public oncology databases in Bioconductor. JCO Clinical Cancer Informatics, 4, 958–971. doi:10.1200/CCI.19.00119

Love, M. I., Huber, W. and Anders, S. (2014). Moderated estimation of fold change and dispersion for RNA-seq data with DESeq2. Genome Biology, 15, 550. doi:10.1186/s13059-014-0550-8

Examples

str(brca_pi3k)
#> List of 2
#>  $ Normal: num [1:100, 1:28] 0.2714 -0.0551 -0.9915 -1.777 -0.6746 ...
#>   ..- attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
#>   .. ..$ : NULL
#>   .. ..$ : chr [1:28] "AKT1" "AKT1S1" "AKT2" "AKT3" ...
#>  $ Tumor : num [1:100, 1:28] -0.41354 0.00299 -0.14622 0.39237 0.96486 ...
#>   ..- attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
#>   .. ..$ : NULL
#>   .. ..$ : chr [1:28] "AKT1" "AKT1S1" "AKT2" "AKT3" ...
#>  - attr(*, "genes")='data.frame':	28 obs. of  3 variables:
#>   ..$ Gene   : chr [1:28] "AKT1" "AKT1S1" "AKT2" "AKT3" ...
#>   ..$ og_tsg : chr [1:28] "OG" "OG" "OG" "OG" ...
#>   ..$ pathway: chr [1:28] "PI3K" "PI3K" "PI3K" "PI3K" ...
head(attr(brca_pi3k, "genes"))
#>       Gene og_tsg pathway
#> 1     AKT1     OG    PI3K
#> 2   AKT1S1     OG    PI3K
#> 3     AKT2     OG    PI3K
#> 4     AKT3     OG    PI3K
#> 5 EIF4EBP1     OG    PI3K
#> 6  MAPKAP1     OG    PI3K
sapply(brca_pi3k, function(m) round(mean(apply(m, 2, sd)), 2))
#> Normal  Tumor 
#>   0.69   1.00
